Article Title: Nominee vs legal heir: What is the difference and who has claim on assets? All you need to know
Article Text:
AI image

Who is a Nominee?



Who is a Legal Heir?

Difference between a Nominee and a Legal heir

Aspect Nominee Legal Heir Role Custodian Owner Transfer of Assets Can be done without any legal formalities. Requires testamentary documents for proof of ownership. Powers No power to transact, use, or transfer assets. Power to use and transact assets as an owner. Appointment Owner can appoint anyone, but some institutions specify certain conditions. Determined by succession/personal laws. Legal Right Cannot contest ownership legally. Can contest ownership in a court of law.

When individuals open bank accounts, invest in mutual funds, or buy insurance, they are often asked to name a nominee.However, many people mistakenly assume that the nominee automatically inherits the assets. In reality, the nominee is not always the final recipient — the ownership rights belong to the legal heir, reported ET.Understanding the distinction between these two is essential to ensure that your wealth is passed on to the intended beneficiaries.A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets.The nominee’s role is limited to holding and managing the assets until they are legally transferred to the rightful heirs.According to ET, the nominee cannot sell, trade, or make any transactional decisions about the assets.The account or policy owner can appoint anyone — family, friends, or acquaintances — as a nominee, though financial institutions often prefer close family members.In some cases, the nominee and the legal heir can be the same person, which helps in ensuring a smoother transfer of assets.The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away.To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will or other testamentary proof.If there is no will — a situation known as dying intestate — the heir is determined as per the country’s succession or personal laws, reported ET.While a nominee can initially access the assets, only the legal heir can claim them permanently or challenge ownership in court.Experts quoted by ET emphasise that having clarity on this difference helps avoid disputes and ensures that the savings reach the intended family members or beneficiaries.Therefore, it is advisable to regularly update both nominees and wills to align with one’s estate planning goals.
Article Summary: A nominee acts as a temporary custodian of the deceased person’s assets. The legal heir or beneficiary is the rightful owner of the assets once the original holder passes away. To claim ownership, the legal heir must produce valid documents such as a will.

How Jeevan Pramaan simplifies pensioner verification



Every year, lakhs of pensioners across India must prove that they are still alive to continue receiving their pension. This verification, known as the Life Certificate or Digital Life Certificate (DLC), is a crucial and mandatory step in ensuring that pension payments are made only to eligible recipients, preventing fraud and misuse.Traditionally, this process involved visiting the bank or pension office in person, standing in long queues, and submitting a signed paper certificate. However, with the government’s focus on digitisation and technological advancement, this process has become much simpler, faster, and more convenient. Pensioners can now submit their certificates digitally from the comfort of their homes using Jeevan Pramaan, a secure, user-friendly, and Aadhaar-based platform.A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries.The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric-enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.Introduced by the Government of India, it uses Aadhaar-based biometric authentication using either fingerprint or iris scan to verify a pensioner’s identity. Once verified, a digital certificate is automatically generated and shared with authorised pension disbursing agencies.This online process eliminates the need for physical verification, providing elderly pensioners with a simpler and more accessible way to maintain their pension benefits.According to PIB, The submission of the Life Certificate is mandatory for all pensioners who wish to continue receiving their pension without interruption. For the year 2025, the standard submission period is betweenTo make the process more comfortable for the elderly, the government allows pensioners aged 80 years and above to begin the submission process earlier, from 1 October 2025. This extended window gives senior citizens more time and flexibility to complete the procedure without facing last-minute difficulties.The Jeevan Pramaan process involves two main steps: registering the biometric device and generating the digital certificate.Before using the service, pensioners or operators must register their biometric device such as a fingerprint or iris scanner. During registration, the user provides their Aadhaar number and mobile number, after which an OTP (One-Time Password) is sent to their mobile. After entering the OTP, they must provide their name and email ID before scanning their fingerprint or iris.Once authentication is complete, the system confirms that device registration was successful, allowing the user to move to the next step.In this step, the pensioner enters personal details such as Aadhaar number, mobile number, name, PPO number, pension type, sanctioning authority, disbursing agency, and bank account details. The system also asks whether the pensioner has remarried or is re-employed.After entering all details, the pensioner scans their fingerprint or iris using the registered biometric device. Upon successful authentication, the Digital Life Certificate is generated, and an SMS acknowledgment with the Jeevan Pramaan Certificate ID is sent to the registered mobile number.This certificate is automatically stored in the Life Certificate Repository, accessible anytime to both pensioners and pension agencies.Once the Digital Life Certificate is created, it can be electronically delivered to the concerned Pension Disbursing Agency (PDA). PDAs can log in to the Jeevan Pramaan portal to view, verify, or download the certificate directly.Pensioners can also download a PDF copy of their certificate by visiting the Jeevan Pramaan website and entering their Pramaan ID or Aadhaar number. This ensures transparency and easy access for future reference.The government provides several options to submit the Life Certificate, allowing pensioners to choose the method that suits them best.Pensioners who prefer traditional methods can visit their bank branch or a Citizen Service Centre (CSC) to submit their Life Certificate physically. Trained staff at these centres assist pensioners in verifying their details and completing the process.For those unable to travel due to age or health issues, India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) offers a doorstep banking service. Pensioners can schedule an appointment, and an IPPB representative will visit their home to complete the submission using biometric authentication. This service is available for both IPPB and non-IPPB account holders.For pensioners comfortable with technology, the Jeevan Pramaan portal provides a completely online process. By visiting https://jeevanpramaan.gov.in, pensioners can submit their Digital Life Certificate using a computer, laptop, or smartphone equipped with a fingerprint or iris scanner.The system uses the Aadhaar platform to authenticate biometric details. Once verification is successful, a Digital Life Certificate is generated and stored in a secure online repository. Pension disbursing agencies can then directly access the certificate, removing the need for physical paperwork.The UMANG (Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance) app offers another easy option. Pensioners can download the app from the Google Play Store, search for “Jeevan Pramaan,” and select “Generate Life Certificate.”After entering the necessary details such as Aadhaar number, PPO number, and type of pension, pensioners must authenticate themselves using biometric verification. The app then generates a Digital Life Certificate (DLC), which is automatically shared with the pension disbursing authority.All pensioners who receive government, defence, or private sector pensions through authorised disbursing agencies are required to submit their Life Certificate every year. This includes:Failure to submit the certificate within the stipulated period may result in temporary suspension of pension payments until verification is completed.To ensure a smooth submission process, pensioners should keep certain details and documents ready. These include:Having these details ready helps to avoid delays or errors during authentication, whether submitting online or offline.Yes, an Aadhaar number or Virtual ID (VID) is mandatory to generate a Digital Life Certificate. The entire Jeevan Pramaan system is based on Aadhaar authentication, which ensures accuracy and prevents fraud. Pensioners must make sure their Aadhaar is linked with their mobile number and bank account before attempting to generate the certificate.The Digital Life Certificate is fully valid and legally recognised under the Information Technology Act. Pension disbursing authorities across India accept it as an official document, equivalent to the traditional paper-based life certificate.Its biometric verification system makes it secure and tamper-proof, reducing the chances of wrongful pension disbursal or misuse of pension funds.Before the introduction of Jeevan Pramaan, pensioners often faced difficulties in submitting their certificates, especially those with health problems or limited mobility. The digital system has removed these challenges, allowing pensioners to submit their verification anytime and anywhere.By integrating biometric technology and Aadhaar authentication, Jeevan Pramaan has streamlined pension management, improving efficiency for both pensioners and government departments. It also enhances transparency and ensures that genuine beneficiaries receive payments on time.
Article Summary: A Life Certificate is an official document that confirms a pensioner is alive. Without it, pension payments are automatically paused by the pension disbursing agency. This verification is essential for preventing fraudulent claims and ensuring that pensions reach the rightful beneficiaries. The Digital Life Certificate (DLC), also known as Jeevan Pramaan, is an advanced biometric- enabled version of the traditional paper certificate.

How to get your CIBIL Credit score without a PAN Card

Factors affecting your CIBIL score

Article Title: Govt to tighten vehicle lighting rules: Low-beam-only bikes, reduced headlamp glare
Article Text:
New vehicle rules may curb high-beam glare, with two-wheelers switching automatically to low beam

NEW DELHI: Automatic headlamps in two-wheelers will soon work only in passing beam (low beam) mode, and buses and other heavy vehicles will have to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather. Also, the use of high-intensity headlamps will be restricted across all categories of vehicles to curb glare, which causes visual discomfort or impairs the vision of other road users.The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, among others, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules, with the new safety norms set to take effect from next April. The amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made given that efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.The automatic headlamp norms would be applicable only for new two-wheelers and not existing ones. At present, the Automatic Headlamp On (AHO) system can switch on both low beam and high beam modes depending on vehicle settings. The proposed rule mandates that when the automatic system is active, the headlamp will be on low beam.As for high-intensity headlamps, the maximum permissible intensity has been reduced from 1.5 lakh candela or cd (official base unit of luminous intensity) to 1 lakh cd for two-wheelers.The maximum permissible intensity for 4-wheelers (cars) has been reduced from 2.25 lakh cd to 1.5 lakh cd.As per studies, white light emitted from headlamps and front fog lamps with higher colour temperatures cause significant glare, leading to discomfort and reduced visibility for other road users. To address this issue, the maximum permissible colour temperature has been restricted to 6,500 Kelvin (K).It has also been proposed that the mounting height of main-beam headlamps be equivalent to that prescribed for passing-beam headlamps.These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India — drivers using headlamps on high beam in urban areas, which can temporarily blind motorists approaching from the opposite direction, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of crashes.TOI has learnt that the new-generation system will also include an audio alert to discourage unnecessary use of high-beam mode on city roads. If a driver manually switches to high beam in urban conditions, the vehicle will prompt them to shift back to low beam.However, the alert will be speed sensitive. Drivers travelling on highways at speeds above 60 kmph won’t receive the warning, since the use of high-beam mode may be necessary on poorly illuminated highway stretches. The feature is intended to promote safer driving behaviour in urban areas while ensuring that highway driving is not adversely affected, officials said.The draft amendments also revise lighting requirements across vehicle categories. Besides restricting use of automatic headlamps to low-beam mode, they update norms for high-end headlamps with adaptive passing beam and adaptive high beam.
Article Summary: Automatic headlamps in two-wheelers will soon work only in passing beam (low beam) mode. Buses and other heavy vehicles will have to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather. Use of high-intensity headlamp will be restricted across all categories of vehicles to curb glare.

Article Title: Godfather of AI Yann Lecun wants AI models to upgrade from writing his essays to solving this 'big bedroom problem'
Article Text:
Yann Lecun to Amazon's Jitendra Malik: I don't agree with your definition

AI 'godfather' leaves Meta after 12 years

Meta's former Chief AI scientist who is also popularly regarded as the Godfather of AI, Yann Lecun, wants AI models to do lots more. In a post on X, formerly Twitter Lecun said that he wants LLMs (Large Language Models) to do a lot more including physical work. He made the comment while replying to Paul Graham. "Someone asked what I'd do if I were 17. I'd learn how to build LLMs from scratch, and then train ones as powerful as I could with whatever hardware I could get access to," wrote Graham in a post on X.To this Lecun replied, "I would try to figure out why LLMs can write my essays but not clean my bedroom. Then I would study topics in college and grad school that could help solve that problem. I'll figure out a set of methods and architectures beyond LLMs that can quickly learn to perform physical tasks as efficiently as humans and animals. That last item is also what I would if I were 30, 40, 50, or 66 years old."In a similar context he also replied to his former colleague at Meta Jitendra Malik, who last month left the Facebook-parent to join Amazon's robotics division. Malik wrote, "Scientific terms should have precision.If we use the terms VLM, VLA, WAM in an indiscriminate fashion, as is becoming common in robotics, we are not helping clarity in communication. Let's keep the historical origins of these terms in mind. VLMs arose as multimodal extensions of LLMs-the training was for tasks like VQA (VIsual Question Answering). These capture the static semantics of the scene behind an image. No dynamics. World Models (e.g.@ylecun) Ha & Schmidhuber 2018) on the other hand are primarily dynamics models, which go back to control theory -1960 (Bellman, Kalman etc.) This makes them natural for robotics planning / policies- I am in a state s, what action a should I perform to get to state s'. In classical control, these models were written down a priori by modeling the physics of the system; today we think of them as learned neural networks trained from temporal data e.g. video, robot trajectories. But the concept is the same. We shouldn't mix this concept with VLMs."Amazon exec tagged Yann Lecun in his post. Lecun disagreed with him on his views on LLMs, VLMs and robotics. He said that he does not agree with Malik's definition. "Exactly. We also should not confuse world models, as per your definition, with video prediction or video generation models. Understanding the dynamics of a system in order to control it is not the same as producing cute videos," wrote Lecun.For those unaware, Yann LeCun is a French-American computer scientist widely known as one of the Godfathers of AI. He won the 2018 Turing Award for deep learning, created convolutional neural networks (CNNs), served as Meta's Chief AI Scientist, and is a professor at New York University. In November 2025, Leun announced his planned departure from Meta, the company he has been part of for twelve years. "As many of you have heard through rumours or recent media articles, I am planning to leave Meta after 12 years: 5 years as founding director of FAIR and 7 years as Chief AI Scientist," he wrote. "The impact of FAIR on the company, on the field of AI, on the tech community, and on the wider world has been spectacular," he added.
Article Summary: AI 'godfather' leaves Meta after 12 years as Chief AI Scientist. Yann Lecun wants LLMs (Large Language Models) to do a lot more including physical work. He also replied to his former colleague at Meta Jitendra Malik, who last month left the Facebook-parent to join Amazon's robotics division.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jack Dorsey: “Everyone has an idea. But it’s really about executing the idea and…” - simple lesson about taking the first step
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jack Dorsey

“Everyone has an idea. But it’s really about executing the idea and attracting other people to help you work on the idea.”

What Jack Dorsey meant by the quote

Why having an idea is only the beginning

The role of other people in turning ideas into reality

Jack Dorsey’s early interest in technology

How Dorsey turned a simple payment idea into Square

Execution means testing an idea against reality

Why collaboration can change the original idea

The difference between an idea and a working product

What Dorsey’s quote means for everyday projects

Why the quote remains relevant

Lessons learnt from Jack Dorsey’s quote

An idea needs action to become useful.

You do not have to build everything alone.

Execution reveals what an idea is missing.

The first version does not need to be perfect.

Feedback can make an idea stronger.

Collaboration brings skills and perspectives you may lack.

Simple ideas can require complex execution.

Adaptability is part of turning an idea into reality.

An idea can arrive in a few seconds. It might come while solving a problem at work, talking with a friend, using a product or simply wondering whether something could be done differently. Most people have ideas from time to time, but very few ever turn them into something real. The difference is rarely just about having a clever thought. An idea needs time, effort, testing and, in many cases, other people who can bring skills that the original creator does not have. That is the thinking behind a well-known observation from Jack Dorsey, the co-founder of Twitter and Square. The quote points to a simple distinction: thinking of something is only the beginning. What follows is the harder process of making it work.Dorsey’s point is not that ideas have little value. An original idea can provide the direction for a product, business or project. But an idea remains theoretical until someone starts making decisions about how it could work in practice.Execution is where those decisions begin. A person has to decide what to build first, what can be left out, what resources are needed and how the idea should change when reality does not match the original plan.The second part of the quote is just as important. Dorsey refers to attracting other people to work on the idea, recognising that large projects rarely depend on one person alone. Different people may bring technical knowledge, design skills, business experience, funding, contacts or an understanding of customers.Ideas are easy to discuss because they have no practical limitations yet. Once someone tries to build one, those limitations become visible.A product may cost more than expected. A technical problem may force a redesign. Customers may not respond as anticipated. Something that seemed essential might turn out to be unnecessary.This is why execution can change an idea rather than simply reproduce it. The original concept provides a starting point, while the process of building reveals what actually works.A founder may have the initial concept, but that does not mean they possess every skill needed to develop it.A software project might require programmers, designers, product managers and people who understand the market. A physical product could need engineers, manufacturers and distributors. Even a small personal project can become easier when someone else brings knowledge or experience that the creator lacks.Dorsey’s wording about “attracting” people also suggests that collaboration cannot simply be assumed. Others need to understand the purpose of the project and see a reason to contribute.Dorsey was born in St Louis, Missouri, in 1976 and developed an interest in computers while growing up. He became particularly interested in communication and dispatch systems, including the way information could be shared quickly between people working in different locations.That interest later became relevant to the technology projects he pursued. He studied at the Missouri University of Science and Technology before attending New York University, although he left university without completing his degree. He subsequently worked as a programmer and became involved with software relating to dispatch and real-time communication.His early career was not built around a single grand plan. Instead, several interests gradually came together around software, communication and the movement of information.Dorsey later applied his interest in communication and technology to a very different problem.In 2009, he co-founded Square with Jim McKelvey. The company developed a small card reader that could connect to a mobile device, allowing businesses and individuals to accept card payments without relying on traditional payment terminals.The device looked simple, but the system behind it was not. Payment technology involves security, financial regulations, software, hardware and relationships with financial institutions.Square eventually expanded beyond its original product into a broader range of financial services. The company changed its corporate name to Block in 2021.The contrast between Twitter and Square is useful when considering Dorsey’s quote. The initial concepts for both companies could be explained relatively simply. Building businesses around those concepts required considerably more work and the involvement of many other people.Execution is often treated as simply completing a plan. In practice, it can mean discovering that the original plan needs to change.A prototype may reveal a technical problem. Early customers may ask for something unexpected. A product that looks useful may prove difficult to operate at scale. These experiences provide information that cannot always be gained through planning alone. That is why the first version of a product does not have to be perfect. It can serve as a way of finding out what works, what does not and what needs to be changed before more resources are committed.Bringing other people into a project introduces different perspectives.A programmer might identify a technical limitation that the founder had overlooked. A designer might notice that the product is difficult to understand. Someone working with customers might discover that the problem being solved is slightly different from what the team originally assumed.These disagreements can be useful when they are handled constructively. The final product may therefore contain ideas that were not present in the original concept. That does not necessarily mean the initial idea failed. It can mean the idea developed as more information became available.There is a natural temptation to focus on the moment an idea is conceived. It feels like the creative part, and it can be exciting to imagine what something might become. The less visible work comes afterwards. Someone has to build the first version, find out whether people want it, correct mistakes and keep improving it. If the project grows, more people become involved and the work becomes divided across different areas.At that stage, the original idea is still important, but it is no longer the whole project.The principle does not apply only to technology companies or entrepreneurs. Someone may have an idea for improving a process at work, starting a community project, creating a small business or learning a new skill. The same question eventually appears: what is the first practical step?It may be as simple as making a prototype, speaking to potential users, writing down the requirements or finding someone with the missing expertise. Starting small can also make an idea easier to evaluate. Instead of trying to prove that the entire concept will work, a person can test one part of it.Ideas have become easier to share, but turning them into functioning products, businesses or projects still takes practical work.Dorsey’s experience reflects that gap. Twitter began with a relatively simple communication concept, while Square started with a straightforward approach to accepting card payments. Both eventually required large teams and complex systems.His quote captures the distinction in simple terms. Having an idea is common. Making it work requires execution, and building something substantial often requires other people willing to take part in the process.
Article Summary: Jack Dorsey is the co-founder of Twitter and Square. He said: ‘It’s really about executing the idea and attracting other people to help you work on the idea’ An idea needs time, effort, testing and other people who can bring skills that the original creator does not have.

Article Title: Apple’s first foldable iPhone may take a step back from using standard feature for authentication
Article Text:
Apple foldable iPhone may launch at $2,000

Apple’s first foldable iPhone: Key hardware omissions but premium pricing

Apple is likely gearing up to introduce its first-ever foldable iPhone at an upcoming launch event targeted on or around September 9, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has said, revealing some of the key details which indicate that the phone may compromise on certain standard premium features, notably swapping facial recognition for older biometric authentication.According to Gurman, rather than featuring the company's established Face ID system, the foldable design relies on Touch ID for user authentication. While returning to fingerprint scanning may feel like a step backward to some modern smartphone owners, many users remain comfortable with Touch ID across current Mac computers and iPads, he said.The foldable iPhone will function as an ultra-premium flagship with retail pricing expected to exceed $2,000. However, early impressions highlight a significant hardware omission, Gurman said.Despite excelling as an expanded camera viewfinder, the initial model lacks a telephoto camera for optical zoom. Given that the target audience willing to pay more than $2,000 closely overlaps with users demanding top-tier camera versatility, omitting advanced zoom could impact early sales.Citing testers who have handled the hardware, Gurman said that the device fits comfortably into pockets, highlighting the durability and feel of the sophisticated hinge system alongside new iPad-style multitasking interfaces optimized for the large internal screen.The form factor enables users to switch between regular single-handed tasks, such as texting or making quick phone calls, and an expansive display suited for video streaming, mobile gaming and other work.Increased consumer awareness could simultaneously benefit Android manufacturers like Samsung and Google, whose offerings feature larger screens and mature folding hardware that some buyers may view as higher-tier alternatives.
Article Summary: The foldable iPhone will function as an ultra-premium flagship with retail pricing expected to exceed $2,000. The initial model lacks a telephoto camera for optical zoom. The device fits comfortably into pockets, highlighting the durability and feel of the hinge system alongside new iPad-style multitasking interfaces.

Article Title: Slack Code puts AI coding agents in the group chat, and everyone gets to watch
Article Text:
Slack Code puts Claude, Devin, Copilot and ChatGPT into shared channels where the whole team can watch, steer and approve the work before it ships.

Slack says writing code stopped being the hard part

Slack has launched Slack Code, a product that drags AI coding agents out of private terminals and into shared channels where the whole team can follow along. Tag an agent like Anthropic's Claude, Cognition's Devin, GitHub Copilot, ChatGPT or Vercel's agent from any conversation, and it spins up a project-specific code channel to take on the job. That channel carries its own tabs for the conversation, the plan, the code diffs and a live HTML preview of what the agent built. Once the task is finished, the channel archives itself and leaves behind a searchable audit log.The feature went live on August 20 and works on every Slack plan, including free ones. The catch is that access to each partner agent is bought separately, which tells you exactly where Salesforce expects the money to sit. Slack calls the idea "multiplayer AI," and the pitch is that a product manager, a designer and an engineer can all steer the same agent without anyone opening a terminal."Code is no longer the bottleneck," Rob Seaman, Slack's interim CEO, said in a press briefing. "Ideas, taste, judgment, craft, those are the things that are the bottleneck." Cognition backed the velocity claim with its own numbers, with president of new enterprise Jeff Wang saying merged pull requests jumped tenfold in recent months while headcount rose about 40 percent.The obvious worry is AI slop arriving at scale. Slack VP of product Katie Steigman argues visibility is the fix rather than the problem, since colleagues can see your intent and tell you the output is weak before it ships. Her own habit is to tag an engineer on every pull request she opens.On security, agents inherit the permissions of whoever invokes them. Seaman was blunt that there are no god permissions or bot-level access, and that a code channel only hands the agent context from the conversation that triggered it. Merging to production still needs human sign-off inside the channel.Slack is also shipping agent DMs, a new Agents tab with live status and a stop button, and an Add to Slack flow for agents built on Lovable, n8n and LangChain. The code channel APIs open to outside developers later, with marketing and legal work named as the next targets.
Article Summary: Slack has launched Slack Code, a product that drags AI coding agents into shared channels. The whole team can watch, steer and approve the work before it ships. Slack calls the idea "multiplayer AI," and the pitch is that a product manager, a designer and an engineer can all steer the same agent.

Article Title: Judge accused of relying entirely on AI still protected from lawsuit, US court rules
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation purposes only

What judicial immunity means in the case

Judges may still face other challenges

A US federal court has ruled that a judge accused of relying entirely on AI to make a court decision can still be protected by judicial immunity. This could mean that the judge cannot be sued over the alleged AI use. According to a report by Tom’s Hardware, the decision comes from Phillips v. Parlade, a case decided by US District Judge Gloria Navarro of the District of Nevada. The plaintiff, Phillips, argued that judicial immunity should not protect the state judge because she allegedly handed over her decision-making duties completely to AI.In the lawsuit, Phillips claimed that if the judge had delegated 100% of the decision-making to artificial intelligence, the resulting order could not be considered a judicial act based on the judge's own judgment.He also argued that such complete delegation meant the judge had acted outside her legal jurisdiction, which can be an exception to judicial immunity. Judge Navarro rejected those arguments.US judges generally have broad protection from civil lawsuits over actions taken in their judicial role. That protection can apply even when a judge is accused of making mistakes, acting with bad motives or going beyond their authority.Exceptions exist. That immunity may not apply when the judge acts in total absence of jurisdiction or when the act complained of is not a judicial act.Courts generally consider several factors when deciding whether an action is judicial. These include whether it is a normal part of a judge's duties, whether it happened in chambers, whether it involved a case before the judge and whether the judge was acting in an official capacity.In this case, the federal court found that issuing a decision in a pending case was clearly part of a judge's normal duties. Phillips also did not claim that the decision was made outside the judge's chambers or provide legal support for the argument that AI use placed the judge outside her jurisdiction.As a result, the court concluded that judicial immunity still applied and dismissed the lawsuit.The ruling, however, does not prevent litigants from challenging a judge's actions through other legal channels. According to the report, a person can appeal a decision through the state court system, seek other available legal remedies or file a disciplinary complaint against the judge.The case therefore leaves a key question open: “what legal or ethical rules should apply if a judge actually delegates judicial decision-making to an AI system?,” the report states.
Article Summary: US judges generally have broad protection from civil lawsuits over actions taken in their judicial role. That protection can apply even when a judge is accused of making mistakes, acting with bad motives or going beyond their authority. That immunity may not apply when the judge acts in total absence of jurisdiction or when the act complained of is not a judicial act.

Article Title: A tech enthusiast spent 3 years testing 351 microSD cards, and 177 have already failed
Article Text:
351 microSD cards, 3 years, 133 petabytes written: 177 are already dead

PNY, Kingston and Delkin top the consumer microSD card rankings

SanDisk and ADATA cards died far sooner than their reputation suggests

High endurance microSD cards did not earn the price premium

What this microSD endurance test cannot tell you

A tech enthusiast has spent three years writing data to microSD cards until they die, and the pile of casualties is now big enough to say something useful about which brands actually survive. Matt Cole, who posts as mikaey00, owns 351 cards covering 111 models from 52 brands. Of those, 177 are dead, 107 are still being tested, and 67 sit on a shelf waiting for a card reader to free up.The scale is hard to picture. Cole's machines have pushed more than 133 petabytes of writes through these cards and finished over 4.6 million program-verify-erase cycles. A card counts as failed when it stops working, makes itself read-only, or shows verification errors across at least half its sectors. He posted the third anniversary update to Reddit's r/DataHoarder, where it pulled close to 6,000 upvotes.The average consumer card in the test has lasted around 10,000 cycles. PNY sits at the top with 10 cards averaging 643 days and 15,700 cycles, and its PRO Elite Prime landed in the top 10 percent for every performance measurement Cole took. Kingston's 12 cards averaged 694 days and roughly 23,500 cycles, with the Canvas Select Plus 32GB still running after nearly the full three years.Delkin's HYPERSPEED 128GB took more data written per card than any other consumer brand and posted the fastest random write speeds in the collection. Lexar and Samsung round out the top five. Amazon Basics 64GB cards have not failed at all after 788 days and 4.2PB written, but Cole left them out of the rankings because Amazon can swap the NAND without changing the product name.The bottom of the list is more surprising. Walmart's onn 32GB cards averaged 40 days and 1,400 cycles. ADATA's Premier 32GB managed 2,350 cycles, Gigastone lasted 114 days on average, and none of Cole's nine Silicon Power cards reached 4,000 cycles. SanDisk gets a dishonorable mention as the biggest brand in the collection. Of 28 consumer cards, only five are still alive, at an average of 384 days and 9,404 cycles.This is the finding buyers should sit with. High endurance cards averaged about 14,000 cycles against 10,000 for consumer models, a gap smaller than the marketing implies, and several performed worse. All three SanDisk High Endurance 64GB cards are dead. Kingston's High Endurance 32GB quit after an average of 143 days. Industrial cards are the real step up at roughly 122,000 cycles, with Kingston's Industrial 8GB hitting 141,600. The oddity is a single Hiksemi NEO 8GB, an ordinary consumer card, which has cleared 143,800 cycles and is still going.Cole runs the project on a shelf of mini PCs and old gaming laptops, including a Beelink Mini-S, five TRIGKEY Green G4 units and an Asus ROG Strix Hero II. He buys most of the cards himself, and rising memory prices are making the hobby expensive.None of this predicts how long a card lasts in a phone or a Steam Deck. It is a torture test. What it does show is that the badge on the packaging is a weaker signal than three years of writes.
Article Summary: PNY, Kingston and Delkin top the consumer microSD card rankings. High endurance cards averaged about 14,000 cycles against 10,000 for consumer models. Amazon Basics 64GB cards have not failed at all after 788 days and 4.2PB written.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Snapchat CEO Evan Spiegel: “It’s not about working harder; it’s about…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Evan Spiegel

“It’s not about working harder; it’s about working the system.”

Understanding the meaning behind today’s quote

Why effort is not always the problem

How Evan Spiegel built Snapchat around a different idea

The difference between a shortcut and a better process

What this can mean for a career

How to put the idea into practice

Lessons to learn from Evan Spiegel’s quote

Look for the cause, not just the problem

Do not confuse busyness with progress

Improve processes you use repeatedly

Learn how the system works

Question routines that no longer make sense

Use technology to support better processes

Know when hard work is still necessary

Focus on long-term efficiency, not just immediate results

Find ways to prevent the same problem from returning

Work smarter without treating effort as unimportant

Most people have days when the amount of work seems to grow faster than the time available to finish it. A task takes longer than expected, a simple job turns into several smaller ones, and something that was completed yesterday somehow needs attention again today. The usual response is to keep going. Work a little later, move a little faster and try to clear the next item on the list. Sometimes that is necessary. But there are situations where the problem is not how much effort is being put in. It is the way the work has been arranged. A process may be unnecessarily complicated, a routine may have outlived its purpose, or the same problem may be quietly repeated without anyone questioning why it happens. That is where Evan Spiegel’s observation offers a different way of looking at work and productivity.Working harder is easy to understand. It can mean staying longer, taking on more work, responding more quickly or simply putting greater effort into the same routine.Working the system is different. It means understanding the process around a task and looking for the part that can be improved.If an employee spends an hour every day fixing the same type of mistake, the answer may not be to become better at fixing it. The more useful question could be why the mistake keeps being produced.That distinction matters because individual effort has a limit. A better process can continue producing benefits after the original change has been made.Workplaces tend to reward visible effort. Someone answering emails late at night or completing a large number of tasks can appear highly productive. Less visible is the person who changes a process so those tasks no longer take as long.This can create an odd situation. A worker may become extremely good at dealing with an inefficient system without ever questioning the system itself.There is nothing inherently wrong with hard work. Some jobs demand it, particularly when deadlines are tight or circumstances are difficult. Spiegel’s point is more specific: when a problem repeats, simply increasing effort may not be the most effective response.Evan Spiegel became one of the most recognisable figures in social media after co-founding Snapchat with Bobby Murphy and Reggie Brown while studying at Stanford University.Snapchat took a different approach to online communication. Photos and messages could disappear rather than remain permanently visible, challenging the expectation that everything posted online needed to become part of a lasting digital record.The service grew rapidly and eventually became part of Snap Inc., with Spiegel serving as chief executive. The company expanded its platform through features including Stories, Discover and augmented-reality lenses.“Working the system” can sound as though it means finding a loophole. That is not necessarily the useful interpretation.A shortcut avoids work. A better system changes how the work is performed.Imagine a customer service team receiving the same ten questions every week. Each employee could continue answering them individually. Another approach would be to identify the recurring questions and create information that addresses them before a customer needs to ask.The work has not disappeared. It has moved to a different point in the process, where it can have a wider effect.For someone early in their career, the temptation can be to prove value by accepting more work. Taking responsibility is useful, but becoming the person who constantly fixes the same problems can eventually become limiting.Learning how a workplace operates can be just as valuable as learning how to perform a particular task.Who makes the decision? Where does information get held up? Which tasks are repeated? What requires approval, and does that approval actually change the result?These are practical questions. They can also reveal where someone's time is being consumed.A useful starting point is to watch for repetition.If the same mistake, delay or administrative task appears regularly, stop for a moment before simply dealing with it again. Look at where it begins. Consider who touches the work before it reaches you. Check whether information is being entered more than once. Ask whether a step exists because it is genuinely necessary or because it has simply remained in place.The aim is not to redesign every part of a working day. Sometimes a small adjustment is enough.A template, an automated task, a clearer instruction or a change in who approves something can remove a surprising amount of repeated work.
Article Summary: Evan Spiegel co-founded Snapchat with Bobby Murphy and Reggie Brown. The company expanded its platform through features including Stories, Discover and augmented-reality lenses. Spiegel's quote offers a different way of looking at work and productivity. Do not confuse busyness with progress, and work smarter without treating effort as unimportant.

Article Title: Melinda French Gates who called divorce with Bill Gates one of her life’s most difficult transitions; said: I want to tell everyone to take
Article Text:
Melinda French Gates on divorce and life changes: I want to tell everyone to take

“I want to tell everyone to take time in quiet,”

Melinda French Gates on self-care during major transitions

“Don’t just leave and then jump to the next thing,”

Mental health and work-life balance

Melinda French Gates has spoken about the role of self-care during major life changes, drawing on experiences from motherhood and her divorce from Microsoft cofounder Bill Gates. In her 2025 book The Next Day: Transitions, Change, and Moving Forward, French Gates called her separation one of her life’s most difficult transitions and shared advice for people navigating periods of change.she told Forbes last year, encouraging people to put down their phones and spend 10 minutes a day on self-care. She suggested activities such as meditation, jogging or other forms of wellness as ways to create time for themselves.French Gates said she first understood the importance of taking time for herself during the early years of motherhood. Between carpools and caring for her three children, she found moments to step away, including when her children were napping and early in the morning.She initially found it difficult to prioritise her own wellbeing while her children were young and required much of her attention. Over time, however, she said she realised that making time for herself could also help her become a better mother.French Gates shares three children with Bill Gates.
